newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-prosecutor in Mexico's Salinas case arrested.
newsitem.headline: Ex-prosecutor in Mexico's Salinas case arrested.

text.p: The former Mexican prosecutor who ordered the arrest of ex-president Carlos Salinas's brother for murder was himself arrested on Thursday in connection with body-snatching and bribery allegations, government sources said.
Pablo Chapa, who has been on the run for three weeks, was arrested in the central town of Jiutepec and was being taken to Mexico City, the sources said.
"The details will be released in the official statement" later on Thursday, a police source said.
Another government source, who declined to be identified, also said Chapa had been arrested in Jiutepec.

Family members said Chapa's lawyer was denying he was under arrest. Chapa has said he was willing to voluntarily turn himself in to authorities if human rights observers were present to ensure he was treated correctly.

Chapa was fired from his job as special prosecutor at the Attorney General's Office in December following a bizarre turn in his probe of the September 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a top leader of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Chapa was in charge of the exhumation of a skeleton at a ranch used by Raul Salinas which investigators claimed was the body of a missing legislator wanted in the Ruiz murder.
The body turned out to be someone else's and was planted by a witch and soothsayer helping Chapa with the probe.

The witch, known as "La Paca," is under arrest on body-snatching charges following revelations that the body belonged to a dead relative whom she and other family members had dug up from a local cemetery and reburied at the ranch.
Chapa was also wanted on charges that he made illegal payments to witnesses in the case.
His former boss, ex-Attorney General Antonio Lozano, was also making a voluntary statement to investigators on Thursday on the bribery charges.
Lozano, who was fired in December, has said President Ernesto Zedillo was told about the payments, while government officals say Zedillo did not approve them.
